Lessons.Title: Using a Trundle Wheel to Measure Distances
ExplanationParagraphs: Edulytiks learning objective: Record wheel rotations and compare measured route distances with precision and reproducibility. Independently authored educational tasks using historical OUR/IM Grade 7 source https://im.kendallhunt.com/MS/teachers/2/9/12/preparation.html (2017–2019 CC BY 4.0 lineage); publisher images/assessments not reproduced.

This optional integrated project builds on earlier Grade 7 mathematics and distinguishes computed illustrative answers from authentic student investigations. Teacher review is required for original designs, unit choices, physical measurements, assumptions and written justification; no numeric answer alone constitutes academic acceptance.

KeyConcepts.Title: Task model
KeyConcepts.Definition: D=turns×measured wheel circumference when rolling without slip.
KeyConcepts.Rule: D=turns×measured wheel circumference when rolling without slip.

KeyConcepts.Title: Rate or geometry
KeyConcepts.Definition: Partial revolutions contribute proportionally.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Partial revolutions contribute proportionally.

KeyConcepts.Title: Evaluation of uncertainty
KeyConcepts.Definition: Calibrate on a known reference length before field use.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Calibrate on a known reference length before field use.

WorkedExamples.Method: Define the model and all assumptions, then compute using appropriate units.
WorkedExamples.Check: Recompute numeric result and have a teacher review real-source data, design constraints and evidence when applicable.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent project scaffold 3

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating an uncalibrated homemade wheel as an exact distance standard.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It confuses assumptions, units or the mathematical model needed to complete the project.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Document sources and derive each output from correctly identified measures.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Presenting a correct illustrative calculation as a complete authentic project
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The lesson assesses an actual constructed, measured or justified student artifact.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Require a teacher rubric for original solutions, precision and communication.

SummaryPoints: D=turns×measured wheel circumference when rolling without slip.
Partial revolutions contribute proportionally.
Calibrate on a known reference length before field use.

Lessons.Title: Designing a 5K Course

Independently authored educational tasks using historical OUR/IM Grade 7 source https://im.kendallhunt.com/MS/teachers/2/9/13/preparation.html (2017–2019 CC BY 4.0 lineage); publisher images/assessments not reproduced.

This optional integrated project builds on earlier Grade 7 mathematics and distinguishes computed illustrative answers from authentic student investigations. Teacher review is required for original designs, unit choices, physical measurements, assumptions and written justification; no numeric answer alone constitutes academic acceptance.

KeyConcepts.Title: Task model
KeyConcepts.Definition: Five kilometres equals 5000 metres.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Five kilometres equals 5000 metres.

KeyConcepts.Title: Rate or geometry
KeyConcepts.Definition: Lap count=target distance/lap distance.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Lap count=target distance/lap distance.

KeyConcepts.Title: Evaluation of uncertainty
KeyConcepts.Definition: An authentic route design needs scale map, start/finish logic and field-verified lengths.
KeyConcepts.Rule: An authentic route design needs scale map, start/finish logic and field-verified lengths.
